title: This, That, These and Those
introduction: Practise this and that with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: Use this and that for one thing, and these and those for more than one thing. This and these indicate nearness; that and those indicate distance.
rules: Use this and these for things near you, and that and those for things farther away.
This and that are singular. These and those are plural.
Point to something near you and say This is a ...
Point to something farther away and say That is a ...

grammar.description: More than one thing near you.
More than one thing farther away.

examples.question: Name one nearby mango.
steps: Use this for one near thing.

examples.question: Name one distant bus.
steps: Use that for one distant thing.

examples.question: Name nearby books.
steps: Use these for nearby plural things.

examples.question: Name distant birds.
steps: Use those for distant plural things.

exercises.question: ___ is my cup here. (This or That)
exercises.solution: Use this for one object close to you.

exercises.question: ___ is a mountain over there.
exercises.solution: Use that for one object far from you.

exercises.question: ___ are my shoes here. (These or Those)
exercises.solution: Use these for several objects close to you.

exercises.question: ___ are birds far away.
exercises.solution: Use those for several objects far from you.

exercises.question: This ___ a ruler.
exercises.solution: This refers to one thing, so use is.

exercises.question: Those ___ trees.
exercises.solution: Those refers to several things, so use are.

exercises.question: That is ___ orange.
exercises.solution: Orange begins with a vowel sound, so use an.

exercises.question: These are three ___. (pencil or pencils)
exercises.solution: Three requires a plural noun; add s to pencil.

exercises.question: ___ is a flower beside me. (This or That)
exercises.solution: Beside me indicates a nearby singular object.

exercises.question: ___ are houses across the road. (These or Those)
exercises.solution: Across the road indicates objects at a distance; houses is plural.

summary: This and these are for nearby things. That and those are for things farther away.
